newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close weaker as U.S. market slides.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close weaker as U.S. market slides.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed weaker on Thursday, pulled lower by a drop in U.S. Treasury prices, the weight of new supply and a softer Canadian dollar, analysts said.

"There was a lot of supply today, and over the last couple of days on the bond side. With the U.S. bond market somewhat bearish Canadian bonds are having trouble," said David Ebata, a Canadian market analyst with Boston-based Technical Data.
Canada's 30-year bond fell C$0.85 to C$112.90 to yield 6.926 percent. The U.S. 30-year benchmark bond fell 28/32 to yield 6.65 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds was 28 basis points, unchanged from Wednesday's close.
Canadian bonds softened as U.S. Treasuries broke through key support levels this afternoon amid concern a weaker U.S. dollar would prompt Japanese selling overnight, analysts said.

In Canada, the market also saw the introduction of new supply. The province of Quebec this morning issued a 6.5 percent C$350 million bond due October 1, 2007 in financial markets, lead manager Levesque Beaubien Geoffrion Inc said. The bond was set at C$98.38 with a yield of 6.715 percent for a spread of 41 basis points over Canadian yield curve.

The Government of Canada said this afternoon that it plans to auction on February 26 C$2.7 billion of bonds with an unspecified coupon and maturing on September 1, 2002. The Bank of Canada said it will buy at least C$405 million of bonds.

A weaker Canadian dollar also likely fed the weakness in bonds, said Mark Chandler, senior economist with Goldman Sachs Canada. Chandler said the softer dollar may have been linked to retails sales data out this morning.
Statistics Canada this morning said retail sales fell 0.3 percent in December to a seasonally adjusted C$18.45 billion from a revised C$18.51 billion (C$18.43 billion) in November.
Retail sales were forecast to rise.

In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent bond due 2006 fell C$0.52 to C$105.20 to yield 6.278 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 16/32 to yield 6.38 percent. The negative spread between the bonds was 10 basis points, unchanged from Wednesday.
The three-month cash T-bill traded with a yield of 2.88 percent against the U.S. bill which yielded 5.07 percent.
